source_basis.mapping_rule: One selected source task maps to exactly one source_task turn.

agent_input.workspace_persistence: Reuse the same writable workspace for all turns in this stream; reset only when the declared evaluation condition requires it.

messages.content:
PROJECT NOTES:

Jan 5, 2026
Sophie - Happy to have everyone back from the New Year break. I trust you were all moderate with your indulgences while celebrating. As you know, we have a major project that needs to be completed in the first quarter. We will be seeking a contractor to do the work and Brad will be the main point of contact for identifying the contractor, though I will be involved in the final negotiations. Once the contractor is selected, we will have 18 inches of soil removed from the entire compound, replace with clean soil, and seeded. By the time we begin receiving visitors in mid April, the project needs to be fully completed. I can't say the campus needs to look exactly like it does now, because that won't be possible, but it'll need to look as though it had existed in the final state for some time, such that a visitor would never guess we had just had all of this work done. Bob, Anthony, Ike, and Jase will be the primary laborers for any grunt work that needs done that the contractor doesn't do. Beth will be responsible for securing permits and making sure all of the bills get paid along the way. You won't see much of Coleen and Dale as they will be out drubbing up business for the April event. Marcia will be in charge of compliance considerations, working closely with Beth, and Lissa will be the project manager. If you have any questions, please let me know. 

Brad - I've already identified 4 potential contractors, spoken with one, and plan to make initial contact with the other three today. 

Sophie - Excellent. You're ahead of the game. 

Lissa - Can you send me their names just so I can be in the loop of where you are as we go. 

Brad - Sure thing. 

Beth - Marcia and I were discussing this morning about which permits we think we will need. We are pretty sure on a couple but we may need to do some serious research on this topic. 

Marcia - Actually Beth, I was just thinking, I think you should call the city and ask the building inspector if he could come pay us a visit. I think we should just have him in the loop from the beginning. I'm not sure who the building inspector is, but we'll need him to know what's going on. 

Beth - Good idea, his name is Jack. I'll call over there today. 

Marcia - Sounds good. 

Jase - I know Jack well. He's a good and honest guy. He'll be easy to work with. He actually lives just a few doors down from me and we talk a lot. 

Beth - Cool. 

Sophie - OK, it sounds like we're off to a good start. 

Brad - Sophie, when we settle on a contractor, they'll be able to help us with permit information too. Not saying you shouldn't contact the city guy, just saying that we will not be on our own about this. 

Sophie - Alright. Well that sounds good. Beth and Brad, I think you two are the only ones that have much to do right now as it pertains to this project, the rest of you can go ahead and take care of whatever you have on your plate for today. Thanks everyone. We'll talk again as needed. 

Jan 6, 2026
Brad - (to Lissa and Sophie) - I got ahold of two of the other contractors, Lissa, I sent you an email this morning telling you which ones. I have appointments now scheduled for three contractors, I'm waiting on a call back from the fourth. The first will be here tomorrow at 10:00 AM. The second will come on Friday at 8:30 AM and the third on Friday at 2:00 PM. They are all going to survey the land, understand what we want, and provide us with a bid. 

Sophie - (to Brand and Lissa) - That sounds great. We need to move fast so I appreciate that you got them to come so quickly. 

Sophie - Listen everyone, the first contractor is coming tomorrow to look at the land. Brad and Lissa will work with him...or her....to explain our needs. We have two more coming on Friday. We will get bids from them and go from there. Beth, have you spoken to the city?

Brad - One of the contractors just called and changed the time for Friday. He's coming at 2:30 PM instead of 2:00. 

Beth - Yes, he said he would be happy to come over and talk to us. I asked him if Jan 8 at 3:00 PM would work. He is supposed to get back with me. Sophie, I looked at your calendar and it was open at that time, so I asked him for that time in case you wanted to sit in. I already spoke to Marcia and she is going to join me when meeting him. 

Sophie - I will join you too if that ends up being the time. 

Brad - I just heard from the last contractor. He sounded a little less professional, so I'm not holding out hope. But he'll be here on Monday the 12th at 9 AM. 

Sophie - (to Brad and Lissa) - When you both have a moment, come to my office so we can discuss this fourth contractor. I'd like to know what you mean by saying he sounded less professional. Thanks. 

Jan 7, 2026
Sophie - Brad and Lissa and I met with the first contractor this morning. We were all very impressed. He is going to work up a bid and get back with us. 

Bob - Just curious, I know it's really none of my business, but what did we decide about the trees?

Brad - This contractor thinks he can work around the two large Maples. He said the smaller trees can be uprooted and put back in the ground when the new dirt is poured. If they don't survive, we may have to replace them in the long run. But he feels confident that, with the correct measures, they will survive. The Oak by the parking lot will have to be fully removed. He said we can plant another, but it'll be years before it is as big as the current one. Most of the smaller decorative shrubs will have to be torn out but he said he can replace them like for like. They just won't be as full. 

Bob - Thanks Brad. Have you thought about replacing the smaller trees with something native. Those bradford pears are considered invasive and the state is really pushing for their removal. I hope I'm not speaking out of turn here. Just letting you know. 

Beth - (to Sophie, Lissa, and Marcia) - The guy from the city will be here tomorrow at 3:00 PM. 

Sophie - (to Beth, Lissa, and Marcia) - Great. I'll be there too. 

Sophie - I think Bob is making a good suggestion. I actually saw a news report the other night about the attempt to get rid of the Bradfords. Brad, maybe we should consider that. Can you call that contractor and discuss. We can just tell the others when we meet with them. Also, I was thinking it would be nice to add Hydrangea bushes between the sidewalk and the building. 

Brad - I'll call him and let him know about those things. 

Jan 8, 2026
Sophie - We had a very productive meeting today with the code enforcement officer from the city. His name is Jack, very nice man. He is on board with our project, fully understands our goals, and said we should have no trouble getting city approval. There is a council meeting on Monday night. He is going to present the plan to the city to make sure none of the council people have any concerns or objections. I have spoken to Lissa, Brad, and Marcia. We are all going to attend the council meeting in case there are any questions asked. Also, Brad has now spoken with the first contractor, Premier Landscaping, and has been very impressed with them. We'll see what the bid comes in at, and we have three more to discuss. But so far, things are looking good. 

Jan 9, 2026 
Brad - (to Sophie and Lissa) - Summit Contracting will be here in 30 minutes. Just a friendly reminder. 

Sophie - We met with two more contractors today. The first one was called Summit, and they were fine. I can't say any of us was overly impressed, but we weren't disappointed either. We will see what their bid comes in at. The second one is called Harrison Contracting and Landscaping. They are a husband and wife team. They were very meticulous and friendly. But again, we will need to see what their bid. Turner Buildings and Excavating will be here on Monday. They represent the final bid. Oh and Bob, we took your advice. We have asked each contractor to make a recommendation for replacing the Bradford Pears. Thanks for bringing that to our attention. 

Sophie - (to Beth, Brad, Lissa, and Marcia) - The last contractor that came today mentioned a drainage study. I don't remember Jack saying anything about that. Beth, can you call him and ask him if that is something we are going to need? 

Beth - (to Sophie, Brad, Lissa, and Marcia) - Done. He says no. As long as what we are doing is largely duplicative of what we have, the study will not be necessary. 

Brad - (to Sophie, Beth, Lissa, and Marcia) - Does he know we are having the Oak removed. Not that I think that warrants the study. I'm just curious if we told him. 

Beth - (to Brad, Sophie, Lissa, and Marcia) - I don't remember. I'll reach out to him and make sure he is aware. 

Jan 12, 2026
Sophie - Today we met with the fourth contractor. We are not considering him. He does not meet our standards. So we are down to three. We will wait until we have all three bids and then decide. I hope all of you had a great weekend. Anthony, I understand you got called out on Saturday. Lissa called the customer this morning. Lissa, can you tell us all what the customer said. Thanks for your hard work and dedication Abthony, it's much appreciated. I know it's never easy or fun to get pulled away from your family on a weekend. 

Beth - (to Sophie, Brad, Lissa, and Marcia) - I spoke to Jack and made sure he knew every detail of the plan. He says we will not have to do a drainage study. 

Lissa - She said that she was very impressed by Anthony's kindness and demeanor. She was so thankful that he arrived as quickly as he did. She said he was so helpful and made her feel so important, not a burden. Excellent work Anthony. These are the kinds of interactions that make us shine. 

Anthony - Thank you guys. She was such a sweet little lady. I was happy to help her. 

Jan 13, 2026
Brad - OK, I got the bid from he first contractor. He stated that the current slope of the west lot is not repeatable without pouring concrete under a portion of it. He said there is clearly sink hole activity that has been mitigated by the roots of the shrubs. Since we have to rip out those shrubs, the land is likely to settle greatly below the 18" level. He can fill it with dirt, but it may sink again. He said he suspected it when he was just looking at it with the naked eye. But when the site survey team came to look at it more closely, the recognized the problem. He says we have gotten lucky that that field hasn't fallen in on itself in places. They can sure it up with concrete, but that's going to really increase the cost. If we don't do that though, we may be dealing with sinking ground for years until everything stabilizes. 

Sophie - Damn. I wasn't expecting that. Let's hold off doing anything until we see if the other bids agree with that assessment. 

Bob - Hey Brad, I had this same problem, well, similar problem on my farm. I ripped out a ton of old shrubbery and the whole dang field practically collapsed. I was speaking to a friend of mine who works in home inspections. He said there is a theory that we are in a 100 year drought and the land is just too dry causing it to collapse in on itself. 

Jase - We are also on a very cavernous land. I can't help but wonder if that contributes. Just thinking out loud. I mean think of all the caves that there are around here. 

Jan 15, 2026
Brad - I have received the bid from the guy we don't want to work with. It's $1200 higher than Contractor # 1. I'm just going to start calling them # 1, 2, 3 and 4. Anyway, number 4 is crazy expensive, and he didn't even mention the problem with the west field. Obviously, he's out of the running. I already called him and thanked him for his time. 

Sophie - OK, let us know when you receive the other two. 

Jan 16, 2026
Brad - I received both of the other bids this morning. They are all competitive with one another. Contractor # 3 also called me personally to make sure I received the bid. I told her I had but that I hadn't looked over it yet. She told me all about the problem in the west lot. So she agrees. Number 2 didn't mention it. 

Sophie - OK, well, unless anyone objects, it looks like we're down to number 1 and number 3. Beth, I think you better call Jack and tell him about the problem with the west field. 

Beth - Will do. 

Beth - I just spoke with Jack. He stated that we may need a drainage study based on the new information. He said that we need to pick a contractor and then he wants to come meet with us and the contactor at the same time. 

Dale - I just spoke with Marshall at Apex Interiors. He plans to bring a team of 4 to the April event. 

Sophie - Wrong group chat Dale. 

Dale - Whoops. Sorry. 

Jan 19, 2026
Sophie - (to Brad, Lissa, Bob) - I want us to meet together to discuss the two proposals. Would 3:00 PM today work for all of you? Bob, I know you may be surprised to be included on this. But I would really value your perspective. You have run a farm and worked here for over two decades. I know you know a lot about land management. I think I would be crazy not to include you. 

Brad - (to Bob, Lissa, and Sophie) - I'm free at that time. 

Lissa - (to Sophie, Brad, and Bob) - I can do 3:00 PM. 

Bob - (to Sophie, Brad, and Lissa) - Yes I am happy to sit in on the discussion. I appreciate the invitation. I think I'll be back from my route by then. 

Jan 20, 2026
Sophie - After much consideration, we have decided to accept bid # 3. They are called Harrison. You will likely be seeing a lot of their trucks over the coming weeks. I expect everyone to be as accommodating as possible with them. Beth, I sent you an email with 7 times that work for them and me and Lissa and Brad to meet with them to get going. Can you reach out to Jack at the City and see if any of those times work for him. If we are going to end up needing a drainage study, I really don't want it to prevent the project from being finished by the April event. See what you can do, the fast the better. 

Beth - Done. He will be here tomorrow at 1:30 pm. I hope you don't mind, but to speed things up, I went ahead and called and spoke with Miranda at Harrison. She will be here for the meeting with Jack. I've added it to Sophie, Lissa, Marcia, and Brad's calendar. 

Sophie - Beth, you never ceased to amaze me. Thank you so much. 

Sophie - (to Beth, Bob, Brad, Marcia, and Lissa) - If Bob's calendar is open for that time, add it to his as well. 

Jan 21, 2026
Sophie - Ok everyone, I trust you all saw my companywide email this morning that Ike has put in his two week notice. It's going to be hard to push through without him as he is such an integral part of our operation. It will affect this project too. But I think we can just hire a laborer. Brad, please talk to the contractor and ask them what their expectations are for when they will need us to help the most. We may need to call over to the staffing agency and just hire a laborer for the needed days. Beth, can you please remove Ike from this group. 

Beth - Done.

Brad - Will do. 

Jase - Sophie, I have a son that is currently not working. He's a hard worker. Please understand, I won't be hurt or upset if you don't want to use him. But if you just need someone to do grunt work on some days, he would be a viable candidate. 

Sophie - Jase, send me his information and have him come in to meet with me. 

Jase - Will do. 

Jan 23, 2026
Sophie - I have good news everyone. We had a very productive meeting with the city and with the contractor. We will not need the drainage study. The contractor's bid put a plan in place that satisfied the city. The project is going to cost about $2200 more than we expected. But that's the way things go. Fortunately, everything necessary was in there. 

Bob - That drainage study would have likely cost $800 or more. So at least we didn't get stuck with that. 

Jan 26, 2026
Brad - I have spoken to the contractor. They said we have a choice as it pertains to laborers. If we use their laborers, the cost will increase by $1800. Of course, their bid was based on using our people because that's what we told them we would do. If we use ours, they are going to need the following: 3 people on 3 days, 2 people on 3 days, and 1 person on 8 days. How do you want to handle it. 

Sophie - I met with Jase's son. I think he is a good candidate for all of the days when we only need 1 person. That won't drive up cost any as we will simply pay him what we would have been paying Ike. On the days when we need two people, we can use Jase's son and Jase or Anthony or Bob. The days that we need three people are the biggest problem. I don't think we can be without two of our drivers on those days, one at the most, plus Jase's son. I think we will need to contact the staffing agency for those 3 days. 

Brad - OK, I'll call them. Their workers will cost us more than paying our people because they take out such a large fee. 

Sophie - I know. But we don't have much choice. 

Bob - Sophie, I don't mind to work overtime if that would help. 

Sophie - Thanks Bob, I know you are all ready to do your part. But that's not what I want. I don't want to take you guys away from your families any more than necessary. We will just bring in some laborers from the staffing agency. 

Anthony - Can I say that I am really excited about this. I just think our grounds are going to be so beautiful after this. 

Bob - Did we get a bid on replacing the Bradords?

Brad - That was part of the bids they gave us. Obviously it changed the total compared to reusing them. But it will be so much better. 

Jan 27, 2026
Sophie - Ok everyone, excavation begins tomorrow. There will be an arborist on site, two tractor trailers, two backhoes, and 3 other workers from Harrison. Please be as accommodating and helpful as possible. I have given them the freedom to come inside to use our facilities, but they won't go in any restricted areas, which they have been told about. I told them they can use our break room and bathrooms. I know parking will be tough tomorrow. You may have to park on the street and walk the rest of the way. I know operations will be a nightmare. But I know that you guys will make it work, you always do. Thank you in advance for putting up with the difficulties over the coming weeks. 

Brad - I just got a call from Anthony. He got hurt at a customer's house. He is on his way to the urgent care. 

Sophie - Keep us updated on how he is doing. 

Brad - I am going to call the staffing agency. I think, with Anthony's injury, we are going to need to bring in a laborer from them on all of the days that Harrison's needs more than one of our people. 

Sophie - OK, that'll be fine. 

Brad - Anthony had to get stitches. They said he will be light duty for at least two weeks. He may even need physical therapy afterwards. We will definitely need to fill all of the laborer positions through the staffing agency, except on the days we can just use Jase's son. 

Jan 28, 2026
Brad - On a side note, I have been doing interviews to replace Ike and think I have a good candidate. I know he won't be up and running for a couple of months, but at least it's a start. 

Sophie - That's wonderful. What's his name?

Brad - Jonathan. 

Jan 29, 2026 
Brad - The contractor said that Jase's son is doing a great job. That is really saving us over having to bring in all people from the staffing agency or use Harrison's laborers. Jase, tell him we appreciate him. But there is a problem unrelated to that. The fiber lines were not marked correctly by the internet provider. Fortunately, the men digging saw them and did not hit them or break them. But, they are in a very inconvenient spot. That part of the project is going to be increased by at least 6 hours because of it. So that's going to bring up the final total. 

Sophie - It's always something. Did you contact the internet company to tell them of the mistake?

Brad - No, but I will. 

Beth - By the way, I don't think I mentioned it, but we did secure all permits needed for the entire job. But the city's website shows the permit pricing incorrectly. One of the permits was actually 6 dollars cheaper than the website states. So we saved six bucks. 

Sophie - Well, every dollar counts. 

Jan 30, 2026
Lissa - This is just a friendly reminder that I will be on vacation all next week. Maine, here I come. I offered to keep my cell phone handy but Sophie told me not to answer any calls from this place. So take your troubles elsewhere. Ha! Seriously though, thank you guys for giving me this opportunity and covering for me while I am gone. If you have any questions that you would normally ask me, check with Brad or Marcia. They will help you. 

Bob - Enjoy Lissa. Maine is beautiful. 

Jase - Bring me back the weirdest thing you can find for a dollar. 

Sophie - A well deserved vacation. 

Lissa - Thanks guys. I will Jase. 

Feb 2, 2026
Sophie - As I am sure you all know, we are supposed to get as much as 12" of snow on Thursday. The contractor reports the project is moving along swimmingly. But this will seriously slow things down. We may not have everything perfect for the April event, but we just have to do what we can. Mother nature doesn't consult us, unfortunately. 

Marcia - Will a snow delay affect the cost of the project. 

Brad - I wouldn't think so. But I guess I should call Harrison's and find out. 

Sophie - We'll need to hire someone to plow, but we would need to do that regardless. 

Bob - I can plow it. I have a skid I can mount on my truck. I'll come plow if we get snow. 

Sophie - Thanks Bob. You're amazing. 

Feb 3, 2026
Sophie - Well they've downgraded the storm to 7-9", but that's still more than enough to temporarily derail the project. Bob, are you still good to plow. 

Brad - The contractor said there is no reason the snow should drive up cost, just mess up the deadline. 

Bob - Yep, I'm good to help. 

Sophie - Great. Thank you Brad, thank you Bob. 

Marcia - Has anyone seen if the snow is supposed to hit Maine? I wonder if Lissa will get stuck up there? 

Bob - It's not. It's actually supposed to be 62 degrees and sunny where Lissa is. Go figure. 

Marcia - Well that's a relief. When she hears of our weather she may not come back. 

Sophie - Bite your tongue Marcia. 

Feb 4, 2026
Sophie - The snow is really starting to fall. Anyone who thinks driving home will be dangerous for them, you are free to leave whenever you feel like you need to. 

Marcia - I have plenty of work that I can do from home. I think I will head on home and probably stay there for the rest of the week. My road is really hard to get in and out of when it has much snow on it. 

Sophie - Yes, I've been to your house a number of times. I wouldn't want to make that trek in the snow. Be safe. Text me when you are home to let me know you made it OK. 

Marcia - Will do, thanks. 

Sophie - Bob, are sure you can even get your truck from your house to our lot to plow? You live what, 25 minutes away?

Bob - It won't be a problem. I'll probably wait to plow until about 7:00 AM tomorrow. That way it should be pretty clear when anybody that can make it arrives. 

Brad - I just spoke to the contractor. Under the circumstances, they won't be able to work on the project again until the snow has cleared. I think we can let this chat go dark until that time. We can each peek in on it once a day to make sure nobody has added anything specific to this project. But I don't think there'll be much to say until we have better weather. 

Sophie - Agreed. 

Feb 11, 2026
Brad - The contractor plans to be back on site tomorrow. Make sure you guys accommodate their needs. They don't have a lot of ground to dig up anymore, so the backhoes might be gone in the next week or so. They said there is still a chance that the work will be at least 90% complete by the April event. I was really happy to hear that. Of course, rain or more snow (god forbid) could cause problems. 

Sophie - It will be the rainy season soon. Let's hope for the best. 

Anthony - I know that some of the days where laborers were needed are past. But I'm really feeling pretty good. I only have minor lingering pain from time to time. The doctor said I don't need therapy. I really think I can help if it will prevent you from having to bring in more temporary staffers. 

Brad - Thanks Anthony. We'll play it by ear as those days actually arrive. But either way, I appreciate the fact that you are always a team player. 

Feb 12, 2026
Sophie - Today was a really great day. I spoke with the project manager for the contractor and she said they will be able to finish digging tomorrow. On Monday they plan to prep the ground for putting in new dirt. During negotiations leading up to the bid, we decided to go with grass that can be laid down like turf, already growing out of squares of dirt. That is going to prevent us from needing to seed and wait for the grass to grow. That will make the finished product arrive much faster and, hopefully, have everything looking beautiful and natural for the April event. The contractor commented that everyone here has really been helpful, kind, and accommodating. I appreciate the fact that you guys have gone out of your way to make this a great experience for everyone. 

Bob - It's supposed to be a high of 58 degrees tomorrow, so it should be a nice day for them. 

Feb 13, 2026
Brad - The contractor could use extra help today, likely from about noon to 2:00 pm. I have Jase's son. They need another person though. Are any of our guys available? 

Bob - I am. I was planning to be in house all day today cleaning and repairing recovered equipment. I can help out during that time. 

Brad - Thanks Bob. 

Beth - I got a call from Jack over at the city today. He was just checking in to see how the project is going. I gave him an update, as best as I could. He would like to stop by and see things first hand. Is that OK? Is there a certain time he should come?

Marcia - I can't see why it would be a problem. I think that's pretty standard. 

Sophie - That's fine, Beth. Tell him he is welcome to stop by anytime. 

Beth - Will do. 

Beth - He is coming on Monday. 

Sophie - Thanks Beth. 

Feb 16, 2025
Brad - The contractor thinks they can get all of the dirt put down by Tuesday or Wednesday of next week, barring any weather problems. I looked at the forecast, and it's supposed to be highs in the 40s all week, so I think we should be good. They are calling for snow Thursday night, but only a dusting. I doubt it will have any impact. 

Bob - I really enjoyed working with those guys last week. They are stand-up guys. My schedule looks pretty scant this week, I think I'll be in house most of the week. So if they need help, I can definitely do that. 

Brad - Thanks Bob. They are going to need help with they start putting in the trees, but that will probably be next week or after. 

Anthony - Hey guys, did you see that they found a structural concern with the bridge on HWY B. They are talking about shutting it down. If that happens, we are all going to have to go the long way around to get in and out of here. Fun times. 

Coleen - My brother works for the dept of transportation. He said it's a sure thing. That bridge is going to be shut down today. In fact I was surprised when I came through on my way in this morning and found it was open. I just texted him to see if he has any update. 

Sophie - Brad, can you talk to the contractor and find out if they think that would have any impact. 

Brad - I'm on it. 

Brad - She said it won't matter much. If they shut it down, she'll let the company that is sending the dirt know. They'll just have to adjust the schedule for what time the dump trucks leave the facility. But overall, it shouldn't impact time or price. 

Sophie - Well that's a relief. 

Coleen - There was a typo in the original report. It's not HWY B. It's HWY E. The bridge on the west side of the county. No impact on us. 

Anthony - Sorry about that. The report on Facebook said Y. 

Sophie - Well that's a relief. 

Feb 19, 2025
Brad - Bob, they are going to need your help today if you are available. Just little bits here and there. 

Bob - No problem. I'll be here. 

Feb 20, 2025
Sophie - Well, there wasn't much we needed to talk about this week. Things went well. They are sure the dirt will all be down by the time they go home on Tuesday. It's supposed to rain next Wednesday which will impact how quickly they will be able to start putting down the grass squares. But overall, things are going well. 

Brad - Did Jack ever stop by?

Marcia - Yes, he stopped by last week. I met with him for about 20 minutes. He didn't stay long. He said everything looked like it was coming along "swimmingly."

Brad - Is he British?

Marcia - No. I guess he just likes that word. 

Jase - Brad, my son just texted to ask about his check. He said you guys have been paying him on Fridays but he doesn't see anything in his account today. 

Brad - OK Jase, I'll check into it and message you personally. 

Feb 23, 2025
Sophie - OK everyone, the contractor is already on site. They got started early this morning so they can be sure to have this phase of the project completed by end of day tomorrow. Jase's son will be helping tomorrow but they said they don't need him, or any help today. So you guys can just all go about your normal routines. It's nice now that they've been able to reduce the amount of equipment they have here. I'm glad most of us have been able to park in our normal spots again. 

Brad - Sophie, we have an issue. When they were putting in the dirt next to the lower lot, they noticed that the summit of the lot, right where we park the box truck, is starting to crumble. I went down and looked at it. I don't think it has anything to do with their work. But if we keep parking the box truck there without getting it reinforced, we're going to have a problem. 

Bob - Hey, that section of lot has looked like that for some time and has not been getting particularly worse. I never brought it up because I was watching it and it seemed stable. 

Sophie - If Bob is not worried, then I am not worried. Nevertheless, I think we may want to think about getting bids for overall lot repair and resurfacing. That can be a fall project. 

Brad - That sounds reasonable. Beth, can you call Jack and find out if that requires permits or any city approval?

Beth - Done. He said that if we are doing a simple resurface and minor repairs, the city does not need to be involved. If any significant portions of the lot are being dug up and replaced, he'll at least want to meet with us and whoever we hire to do it, but there still may not be any permits needed. 

Anthony - Hey, I don't mean to speak out of turn, but there is a pretty nice size dent in the side of my work truck. I feel pretty confident it wasn't there on Friday. I had it parked close to one of their trucks when I left on Friday to go home. Remember, I left early, 3:00 PM. I'm not saying they did it. But I'm not saying they didn't. 

Bob - I feel confident the lot will be fine until the fall. 

Lissa - Brad, can you start working on identifying contractors for the lot work, in case we decide to do that?

Sophie - Let's start a new group discussion just for the lot work and keep it out of this discussion. 

Beth - I have started the new discussion. So far, I have Brad, Sophie, Bob, Marcia, Lissa, and myself.

Brad - I'll talk to the contractor about the van. 

Jase - Hey, that dent was there last Thursday. I am sure because I had lunch that day at that picnic table down by that lot. I remember sitting there freezing, because I'm stupid enough to eat outside when it's 43 degrees, and I looked over and saw it. It really stood out to me.
